title: Inverse image preserves sheaf differentials
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common universe of sheaf values, and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits. Let $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ for the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, where ring differentials are those of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; this is a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with the derivation induced by the sectionwise universal derivations. Equip inverse images of rings and modules with the operations induced by the finite-product comparisons of $f^{-1}$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaves $f^{-1}\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{f^{-1}\mathcal B/f^{-1}\mathcal A}$ which carries the inverse image of the universal derivation to the universal derivation. It is natural in commutative squares of sheaves of rings, and its comparisons for identity and composite geometric morphisms agree with the identity and composite inverse-image comparisons.

source.place: Tags 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify) and 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials); naturality and composition are the universal-derivation comparisons in these constructions.

proof.text: Use the explicit relation-map presentation of sheaf differentials. For a presheaf ring map A→B, the free B-module sheaves on B×B, B×B, and A map to the free B-module sheaf on B by the additivity, Leibniz, and base-ring relations. Tag 08TP identifies the cokernel with the sheafification of U↦Ω_{B(U)/A(U)}, and identifies the generator [b] with the universal derivation. Applying this to the given A→B gives the stated model for Ω_{B/A}.

By the exactness lemma for geometric inverse image, f^{-1} on transported abelian/module sheaves preserves the finite limits and cokernels appearing in this relation presentation. By the free-module comparison, f^{-1} of each free f-module term is canonically the corresponding free f^{-1}B-module term, with all canonical generators and finite-product comparisons preserved. Applying f^{-1} to the relation map therefore gives exactly the relation map defining Ω_{f^{-1}B/f^{-1}A}; exactness identifies its cokernel with f^{-1}Ω_{B/A}.

The isomorphism is canonical because it is induced by the unique map between the two cokernels carrying the inverse image of each generator db to the generator d(f^{-1}b). The relation equations (additivity, Leibniz, and annihilation of A) show that this map is well-defined; the same construction in the opposite direction is inverse by the cokernel universal property. Under this identification the inverse image of the universal derivation is the universal derivation.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, compatibility with universal derivations in the displayed cokernel construction

proof.text: For a commutative square of sheaf ring maps, every comparison map in the relation presentations is functorial in the ring maps and in f^{-1}; hence the induced differential isomorphisms commute with the square. For an identity geometric morphism, the comparison fixes every generator and is the identity by cokernel uniqueness. For composable geometric morphisms, both the direct composite comparison and the composite of the two comparisons fix every generator and use the same finite-product and free-module identifications, so they agree by the same uniqueness argument.
